stem:
Walia knows two interior angles of a triangle are $65^\circ$ and $48^\circ$. She wants the third interior angle.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Call the answer a "parallel line" measure, without using the triangle-angle sum.
Subtract $65^\circ+48^\circ$ from $180^\circ$ even if one of those angles were exterior to the triangle, skipping that both known angles must be interior angles of the same triangle.
Use $180^\circ$ minus one known angle alone to name an exterior angle at a vertex, beyond finding the missing interior angle of this triangle.

teacher.key_rationale: Interior angles of a triangle sum to $180^\circ$, so the missing angle is $67^\circ$. Relabeling as a parallel-line measure, dropping the same-triangle interior condition, or stretching into exterior-angle work all miss that hinge.
